title: "Repository structure"
---

# Repository structure

```
research-paper-template/
├── index.qmd                # Guide landing page (this site's home)
├── guide/                   # Handoff guide pages → GitHub Pages
├── paper/
│   ├── paper.qmd            # The manuscript (Quarto, APA-ish sections)
│   ├── _quarto.yml           # Separate Quarto project for the paper
│   └── references.bib        # References
├── R/                       # Reusable helper functions
│   ├── survey-design.R
│   ├── iptw.R
│   ├── lca.R
│   ├── network-analysis.R
│   └── reporting.R
├── analysis/                # Numbered pipeline
│   ├── 00-config.R          # Paths, packages, options (edit me)
│   ├── 01-import.R
│   ├── 02-survey-design.R
│   ├── 03-iptw.R
│   ├── 04-lca.R
│   ├── 05-network.R
│   ├── 06-report.R
│   └── run-all.R            # Runs 00 → 06 in order
├── data/
│   ├── raw/                 # Your input data (gitignored)
│   └── processed/           # Pipeline outputs written here
├── outputs/
│   ├── figures/
│   └── tables/
├── .github/workflows/
│   └── render-guide.yml     # Renders this guide site on push
├── renv.lock
├── CITATION.cff
└── _quarto.yml              # Guide-site project config
```

## Conventions

- **One job per script.** `analysis/NN-name.R` does one thing and writes results to `data/processed/` or `outputs/`. Downstream scripts read from disk, so you can rerun any step in isolation.
- **Helpers are functions, scripts are orchestration.** Reusable logic lives in `R/` and is sourced by the pipeline; `analysis/` calls those functions with project-specific arguments.
- **Raw data is sacred.** `data/raw/` is gitignored and never modified in place. Anything derived goes to `data/processed/`.
- **Outputs are disposable.** `outputs/` is regenerated by the pipeline, so it is gitignored too — only the scripts and the manuscript are version-controlled.

## The two Quarto projects

The guide site (`_quarto.yml` at the root, type `website`) and the manuscript (`paper/_quarto.yml`, type `default`) are deliberately separate Quarto projects. The guide is rendered automatically by GitHub Actions; the manuscript is rendered locally by the author. This keeps a long manuscript from cluttering the navigable guide.
